children: traded modestly lower in Europe on Friday after the company said it had identified a new quality defect that ​could reduce ​corrosion resistance inside the ⁠fuselage structure of ​its best-selling A321neo jets.
said it discovered a "deviation" in surface protection on "stringers located at the lower front section of the fuselage," adding that the problem is not a safety concern.

The planemaker said the source of the issue has been identified and contained, a remedy is available, and aircraft can continue to operate since the rework "does not require any disassembly of the stringers."
was facing a quality issue with insufficient corrosion protection on fuselage sections on hundreds of in-service and in-production jets.
The company reaffirmed its existing delivery target of ⁠~870 jets for 2026, compared with 475 handed over between January and August.

The availability ​of a fix should limit any potential impact on deliveries this year, Jefferies analyst Choe Lemarie said in a note, adding that tracking data shows eight deliveries so ​far this week, suggesting that deliveries are "not meaningfully affected at this stage."

title: Airbus finds new quality flaw in best-selling A321neo jet
